why: Owner-curated EaseUI master reference sample (kinetic set). Human-authored and deliberate, which is the bucket that decides whether the tell family is trustworthy: its fatal failure mode is flagging a good designer's choice. Self-contained — no linked stylesheet. Origin: EaseUI/app/public/samples/kinetic/03-hyper-gloss-y3k-chrome.html, copied 2026-08-30, finding count verified identical to source.
reviewNote: Owner-authored page: on his own work the owner's verdicts are ground truth, not mine. Both fp-open rows below are the ones to check first.

verdicts.reason: Measured: the <title> element opens at line 6 and closes at line 358 — 353 lines, 11,028 raw / 9,334 whitespace-normalized characters, holding a leaked generation-prompt dump ("[var-3] Hyper-Gloss Y3K Chrome ... Reference the background from this codebase"). So the long run is real; what is wrong is WHERE it is read from. The rule prints long[0] faithfully. Root cause: html-extractor's emitText gives head metadata role:"body", so non-rendered <title> text is judged as prose. Fix in the extractor with a "metadata" TextRole, not in the rule. (An earlier reading of this row said line 6 is 123 characters and that the document's text was aggregated into one fact; both were wrong — 123 was one physical line of a multi-line element, and emitText emits own-text per element.)
verdicts.message: 1 body run(s) over 400 characters with no container constraint visible to this tier

verdicts.reason: The page really does set `font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif` for body, with JetBrains Mono as the accent. On a sample whose whole identity is 'Hyper-Gloss Y3K Chrome', Inter is the reflex neutral — exactly the thing the rule names. A deliberate face would carry the aesthetic instead of sitting under it.
verdicts.message: Inter is on so many surfaces it no longer carries personality

verdicts.reason: Verified at line 381: `border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08)` carrying a 32px shadow. A hairline edge and a wide soft shadow are two competing treatments of the same boundary — the named tell, present as described.
verdicts.message: 1px border paired with a 32px shadow — two competing edge treatments on one element

verdicts.reason: Line 400 is `animation: scan 8s linear infinite` — a decorative scanline sweep, part of the Y2K chrome aesthetic. Nothing the reader must read is moving. The rule's own message claims 'auto-scrolling content the reader cannot pause', but it matches any 8s infinite animation without checking that CONTENT is what moves.
verdicts.message: auto-scrolling content on a 8s infinite loop the reader cannot pause
